cf.title: COPY (on_error table) saving error info to a table

input.subject: on_error table, saving error info to a table

verdict_reasoning: The goal builds on the existing ON_ERROR soft-error path and no surviving objection is fatal. The design has open points that the list must settle before code review: replication-ondisk-1 (no rule for changing the fixed pg_catalog type under existing typed tables) and maintenance-fit-2 (COPY builds ModifyTable state by hand around an exported ExecInsert). standards-compat-2 and standards-compat-3 are smaller fixable points. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 31 messages were visible.

brief.title: COPY FROM on_error table: save input conversion errors to a table
brief.problem: With on_error ignore, COPY FROM skips malformed rows but keeps only NOTICE output, so users cannot query which lines and fields failed. The author wants each failed row's error details stored in a table. The thread builds on an earlier suggestion by Tom Lane, linked but not quoted.
brief.proposed_design: COPY FROM gets a new on_error value, table, plus an ERROR_TABLE option that names a user-created typed table of the new built-in composite type pg_catalog.copy_error_saving. On each input conversion error, COPY builds a row of error metadata and inserts it through an exported ExecInsert, so constraints and triggers apply. Then COPY moves on to the next row.
user_visible_surface: COPY option value ON_ERROR table, for COPY FROM in text or csv format only.
New COPY option ERROR_TABLE error_saving_table, required with ON_ERROR table and allowed only with it.
Built-in composite type pg_catalog.copy_error_saving with 11 columns (starttime, userid, copy_tbl, filename, lineno, line, colname, raw_field_value, err_message, err_detail, errorcode).
New NOTICE messages giving the count of saved rows and, with LOG_VERBOSITY verbose, one message per saved row.
C API: ExecInsert in nodeModifyTable.c becomes exported.
author_claims: A preliminary lock check at COPY start means error row inserts cannot block or deadlock in the middle of the COPY.
Using a typed table makes table validation simpler, since only reloftype needs to be checked.
Routing inserts through ExecInsert is neater and close to the normal insert path.
The copy_error_saving definition is fixed, and ALTER TYPE on it is rejected.
The starttime column tells apart rows saved by different COPY commands into one table.
brief.thread_state: Nishant Sharma, Kirill Reshke, Andrew Dunstan, Solaimurugan V and Zsolt Parragi reviewed; Zsolt said v13 looked generally good, and the author says the design may not be bulletproof yet. Open at v15: the NOTICE count is wrong when a BEFORE ROW trigger on the error table returns NULL, and the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: No committer has said whether a fixed built-in composite type in pg_catalog is acceptable, given future changes to its columns.
The proposal does not say how a later change to copy_error_saving would work with existing error tables or pg_upgrade.
Kirill's security concern about error table triggers running as the COPY user got no answer and no change of security context.
The proposal does not say whether an insert failure in the error table aborts the whole COPY; the author deferred documenting this.
The proposal does not say how ON_ERROR table works with REJECT_LIMIT, file_fdw, or partitioned and foreign error tables.
No performance numbers are given for COPY with many bad rows.

prior_attempts.title: Handling of the input data errors in COPY FROM
prior_attempts.who_objected: Stephen Frost, Craig Ringer, Peter Eisentraut
prior_attempts.quote: In the end, this isn't an acceptable approach to this problem.
prior_attempts.reason: Catching the error without PG_RE_THROW() skips the cleanup that AbortTransaction() does, such as resetting memory contexts, releasing locks and restoring user and security contexts. Input functions, including ones from extensions such as PostGIS, can do arbitrary work, so this is not safe. Reviewers suggested a subtransaction approach that retries a batch and skips the failed row. Peter Eisentraut returned the patch because it did not do this or a safe 'soft error' scheme, which Tom Lane also judged hard to make safe.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P2 caught input-function errors with PG_TRY() and did not re-throw them. This proposal uses the existing ON_ERROR soft-error path and adds an ordinary executor insert of the error metadata.

prior_attempts.title: Handling of the input data errors in COPY FROM
prior_attempts.quote: After looking at the way you're handling errors, it seems that you've chosen to go precisely the way people were saying that was not admissible: use a PG_TRY block, and when things go south, simply log a WARNING and move on. This is unsafe.
prior_attempts.reason: Michael Paquier returned the entry because the last patch was five months old, no longer applied, and failed "git diff master --check". On the rebased patch, Alvaro Herrera objected that catching errors in a PG_TRY block and only logging a WARNING is unsafe. Out-of-memory, WAL write failures and serialization failures from triggers can leave memory or session state broken until the transaction aborts. Earlier, Peter Geoghegan said a design that uses subtransactions in a way not obvious to the user would be hard to sell to a committer.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 wrapped InputFunctionCall in PG_TRY/PG_CATCH and logged a WARNING. This proposal reuses the soft-error reporting of ON_ERROR ignore, so the unsafe-catch objection does not carry over.

objections.title: Fixed pg_catalog row type makes later column changes break upgrades
objections.failure_scenario: A user creates err_tbl as `create table err_tbl of copy_error_saving` and fills it. A later release adds, renames or retypes a column of copy_error_saving. pg_upgrade or a dump and restore then has to recreate err_tbl as a typed table of a type that no longer matches the saved rows, and the upgrade or the data load fails.
objections.argument: The type is created by system_functions.sql, so each release defines it fresh, but user tables bound to it carry the old layout. Message #15 names this compatibility risk and asks for confidence that the definition will not change. Message #30 then added starttime, so the definition changed during review. Message #14 says a built-in type needs broader consensus, and no committer has given it.
objections.author_must_show: What happens to existing typed error tables under pg_upgrade and pg_dump when a later release changes copy_error_saving, and how is that change carried out?

critic.reasoning: Message #15 names this risk, and v15 changed the column list without saying how existing typed tables would follow. A new patch version could solve it, for example with a stated rule for changing the type, so the severity is fixable.

objections.title: COPY builds its own ModifyTable executor state around an exported ExecInsert
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch changes what ExecInitModifyTable sets up before ExecInsert runs, for example a new ResultRelInfo field or trigger state. COPY's hand-built ModifyTableContext lacks that setup, and no test fails until a user puts an unusual trigger or index on the error table. Then COPY crashes or misbehaves.
objections.argument: Message #19 shows that COPY copies part of ExecInitModifyTable by hand, arguing case by case that partitions, foreign tables, RLS and EvalPlanQual can be skipped. Messages #24 and #25 then found a use-after-close and a trigger-ordering server crash in this code, which shows how easily the two copies drift. ExecInsert also becomes an exported symbol that extensions will start to call. Later ModifyTable changes would have to keep this second caller in sync with nothing to flag a miss.
objections.author_must_show: Can the error-row insert reuse an existing, already supported entry point, so that later ModifyTable changes cannot silently break COPY?

critic.reasoning: Message #19 describes setting up ModifyTable state by hand in COPY, and messages #24 and #25 show a crash and a stale relation in that code. The claim that extensions will call ExecInsert is a guess and should not be used as support.

objections.title: copy_tbl and userid stored as bare OIDs do not survive dump/restore
objections.failure_scenario: An operator dumps a database whose error table holds a week of rejected rows and restores it on a new server. Tables and roles get new OIDs, but copy_tbl and userid keep the old numbers. Queries that join to pg_class or pg_authid then return nothing or name the wrong table, and nothing reports this.
objections.argument: The documentation states there is no dependency on pg_class or pg_authid, and expects only stale values after a DROP. Postgres already has a way to store such references in user tables so they dump as names, for example regclass and regrole. The proposal does not say why plain oid was chosen over these types. Since the error table exists to be kept and queried later, its contents need to round-trip.
objections.author_must_show: Why does copy_error_saving use plain oid for copy_tbl and userid, and not regclass and regrole, given that error tables are kept across dump and restore?

critic.reasoning: The datatype.sgml hunk says the OIDs go stale only after a drop and does not cover dump and restore, which assigns new OIDs. regclass and regrole dump as names, and the thread does not say why plain oid was chosen.

objections.title: ON_ERROR table cannot be combined with REJECT_LIMIT
objections.failure_scenario: A load job runs with `on_error ignore, reject_limit 100` and switches to `on_error table` to keep the rejected rows. COPY then rejects REJECT_LIMIT with a FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED error, so the job must choose between saving errors and limiting them. A badly broken file of millions of lines loads to the end and fills the error table.
objections.argument: Message #26 shows the patch refuses REJECT_LIMIT with ON_ERROR table. Under the current option set, `table` behaves as a variant of `ignore` that also records each row, so the existing limit applies to it in the same way. The proposal does not say why the limit cannot apply here. Having ERROR_TABLE also adds a second required option where one option implying the other would be enough, and the proposal does not justify this either.
objections.author_must_show: Why should ON_ERROR table refuse REJECT_LIMIT, when the limit applies to ON_ERROR ignore and both options skip the same rows?

critic.reasoning: Message #26 quotes the check that rejects REJECT_LIMIT with ON_ERROR table, and the thread gives no reason for it. The remark about ERROR_TABLE being a second required option is weaker and should not carry the objection.

objections.title: Staging table plus pg_input_error_info already gives the same error rows
objections.failure_scenario: A user who wants queryable load errors can COPY into an all-text staging table, then use pg_input_is_valid() and pg_input_error_info() per column to split good rows from bad ones. That puts message, detail and SQLSTATE into an ordinary table they define. If the feature goes in, core keeps a fixed pg_catalog type and an exported ExecInsert for a result users can already build in SQL.
objections.argument: Postgres already ships pg_input_is_valid() and pg_input_error_info(), which use the same soft-error path as ON_ERROR ignore and return the fields the copy_error_saving type stores. The thread does not compare the proposal with this idiom. Message #2 asked why a table is needed at all, and the answer in messages #3 and #5 is about creating the table, not about need. The staging idiom does cost a second write and loses exact line numbers for multi-line CSV fields, so a committer would likely ask whether that gap justifies a permanent catalog type.
objections.author_must_show: Which real loads cannot use a text staging table with pg_input_error_info(), because of size, line numbers or something else, and how common are they?

critic.reasoning: A text staging table with pg_input_error_info() can produce the same error fields, and the thread never compares the two. The material shows no independent user reports that the double write or lost line numbers are a common problem.

other_surviving.title: No committer who owns COPY or the executor has engaged
other_surviving.failure_scenario: The patch is committed with its open questions about the type freeze, trigger security context and insert-failure behaviour still unresolved. When a bug report arrives about error-table triggers or upgrades, no committer knows the design well enough to fix it. The author says the design is not yet "bulletproof".
other_surviving.argument: In 31 messages and 12 CommitFests, the only committer post is a one-paragraph suggestion of typed tables in message #8. Message #14 says a built-in type "would require broader consensus, which is likely difficult to achieve", and that consensus has not been sought. Message #29 defers documenting what happens when an error-row insert fails because the design "may not be completely bulletproof yet". Kirill's security concern in message #16 got no reply.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which committer familiar with COPY and the executor has agreed to the built-in type and the ExecInsert design, and to owning them after commit?

critic.reasoning: The thread shows one committer post, message #8, which declines to comment on the patch in general. This bears on committability and must not count against the merits of the idea.

refuted.title: Fixed pg_catalog composite type has no upgrade path for its columns
refuted.failure_scenario: A site creates `error_log OF copy_error_saving` in version N and fills it. Version N+1 adds, drops or retypes a column of copy_error_saving. pg_upgrade then rebuilds the table's columns from the new type over heap files that use the old layout. A plain dump/restore either fails or silently realigns the columns.
refuted.argument: Users' typed tables take their row layout from a system type that a later release controls. The type already changed once during review, when v15 added starttime (message #30). Message #15 names this compatibility risk, and message #14 says a built-in type needs broader consensus, but no committer has answered. Blocking ALTER TYPE (message #18) freezes the definition today and does not cover the next major release.
refuted.author_must_show: How would a later release add or change a copy_error_saving column without breaking pg_upgrade or dump/restore of existing error tables?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. The claim that dump and restore "silently realigns the columns" is also doubtful, because pg_dump writes a column list in its COPY commands.

refuted.title: Saved OIDs of the role and target table do not survive dump and restore
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator keeps an error table for audit and later moves the database with pg_dump and restore. The userid and copy_tbl values in the old rows now point to no object, or to an unrelated table or role that got the same OID. A join to pg_class names the wrong table, and nothing reports the mismatch.
refuted.argument: The datatype.sgml hunk records userid and copy_tbl as bare OIDs with no dependency, and says only that the value then identifies no existing object. The rows are meant to persist and be queried later, but restore assigns new OIDs, and OIDs can be reused. Because the stored values point at no fixed object, a later query can join them to the wrong row without any error.
refuted.author_must_show: Why store OIDs and not the qualified table name and role name, given that the error rows are meant to outlive the COPY and be moved between clusters?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which names the existing alternative (regclass, regrole).

refuted.title: Error table triggers run with the privileges of the COPY user
refuted.failure_scenario: A low-privileged role owns a shared error table, grants INSERT on it, and adds a BEFORE INSERT row trigger. A superuser's nightly load uses that table with ON_ERROR table. The first malformed input line fires the trigger as superuser, and the trigger can run `alter role ... superuser`. Nobody notices until the role change is audited.
refuted.argument: Kirill raised this in message #16, and nothing in the thread answers it. v8 rejected error tables with triggers (message #18), but v11 started firing row and statement triggers (message #23) without discussing who the trigger runs as. An ordinary INSERT carries the same risk, but here the insert happens as a side effect of bad input to a different target table, so the COPY user is less likely to check the error table's triggers. The docs only say that triggers fire.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should error-table inserts fire triggers as the COPY user, and not either forbid triggers or switch to the error table owner's security context?

critic.reasoning: The scenario is the same as a superuser running INSERT or COPY into a table owned by a less privileged role, where Postgres already fires triggers as the calling user. The COPY user names the error table in ERROR_TABLE, so the patch follows existing practice.

refuted.title: Fixed pg_catalog composite type ties every future release to its column list
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release adds a column to copy_error_saving, as v15 already did with starttime. A user with an error table created OF the old type runs pg_upgrade. pg_upgrade restores the table and re-attaches it to the new type, the column lists no longer match, and the upgrade fails or the table silently loses its typed link.
refuted.argument: Message #15 says a change to the type "could lead to potential compatibility issues" and asks reviewers to be confident it will not change. Between v7 and v15 (message #30) the column list changed anyway. The patch blocks ALTER TYPE on it (message #18), so there is no way to migrate existing error tables. No committer in the thread has accepted a frozen user-facing pg_catalog row type, and the brief lists this as open.
refuted.author_must_show: How does an error table created on release N survive pg_upgrade and pg_dump restore when release N+1 adds or changes a copy_error_saving column?

refuted.title: No user demand shown beyond the existing NOTICE and staging-table workarounds
refuted.failure_scenario: A user loading a CSV with bad rows can already run COPY with on_error ignore and log_verbosity verbose, or load into an all-text staging table and cast with SQL. If those cover most real loads, the project takes on a permanent COPY option and a catalog type that few people use.
refuted.argument: Across 31 messages, no user describes a production load where the per-row NOTICE output or a staging table was not enough. Message #2 asked why a table is needed instead of a log, and the thread answers how the error table should work, not who needs it. The suggestion in message #1 is linked but not quoted. Reviewers who test the patch (messages #20, #22) confirm it works, but that does not show the size of the group that would use it.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users or field reports need queryable error rows from COPY, and why do on_error ignore with verbose NOTICEs or a text staging table not serve them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1, which asks for the same demand evidence and names the stronger alternative. The verbose NOTICE output is not queryable, so it is not a real substitute.

refuted.title: A fixed pg_catalog type is a lasting cost for a narrow gain
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release wants to record another error field, such as the encoding or the COPY source query. It must then change pg_catalog.copy_error_saving, while user error tables built with CREATE TABLE ... OF still depend on the old shape. Upgrades then have to handle both versions.
refuted.argument: Message #14 says a built-in type needs broader consensus, and message #15 states the compatibility risk and asks whether the definition is stable. Message #30 then added starttime, so the definition already changed during review. Every user of an upgraded cluster carries the type and its upgrade rules, while only users of ON_ERROR table gain from it.
refuted.author_must_show: How would a column added to copy_error_saving in a later release work for existing typed error tables and for pg_upgrade?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. The claim that every user of an upgraded cluster bears a cost is not supported, because an unused catalog type costs non-users nothing shown in the material.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: User typed tables take their row layout from the built-in type copy_error_saving, which a later release may change.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: system_functions.sql creates the new composite type pg_catalog.copy_error_saving, and ALTER TYPE on it is rejected.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: gram.y gains the COPY option ERROR_TABLE and the ON_ERROR value table.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Error tables are typed tables of a system type and store copy_tbl and userid as plain OIDs.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: The patch changes tab-complete.in.c for the new COPY options.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: COPY checks INSERT privilege on the error table and fires its triggers as the COPY user.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A fixed catalog type and a second caller of ExecInsert with hand-built executor state must be kept working.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The review notes say v15 switches COPY to single-row inserts in some cases, and the thread gives no numbers.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: A text staging table with pg_input_error_info() gives similar error rows today.

questions: How would a later release add or change a copy_error_saving column without breaking pg_upgrade or dump and restore of existing typed error tables?
Can the error-row insert use an existing supported entry point, so that later ModifyTable changes cannot silently break COPY's hand-built executor state?
Does a failed insert into the error table (constraint violation, trigger error) abort the whole COPY, and is that the intended behaviour?
Which real loads cannot use a text staging table with pg_input_error_info(), because of size, line numbers or something else?
Why does copy_error_saving store copy_tbl and userid as plain oid and not as regclass and regrole?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows both COPY FROM and the ModifyTable executor code. The one committer post, message #8, suggests typed tables and does not review the patch as a whole.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a pg_catalog type whose columns are frozen for existing user tables across all later releases. The owner also signs for keeping COPY's hand-built insert path in step with ModifyTable changes.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted 15 versions since 2024 and keeps moving the entry between CommitFests, which suggests continued follow-up. The author also says the design may not be bulletproof yet.

priority.reason: The thread shows reviewer interest but no user reports, and the 65 KiB patch touches COPY, the grammar and the executor. Two design points, the type's upgrade rule and the insert path, need an answer and a committer's view before more line review helps.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the hand-built executor state, the preliminary lock check and the single-row insert mode in v15 could not be checked. Messages #4 to #31 were seen only through the objections' references.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve handling of OOM errors in libpq making process hangling for COPY and bind (take 2)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes libpq hangs on out-of-memory errors while it parses COPY start and ParameterDescription messages. The parser leaves pqParseInput3 on error and keeps the first error message, so PQgetResult and PQexecFinish return the failure and do not wait for server input that will not come.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas committed the ParameterDescription fix but did not commit the COPY part. He could not see why the PQexecFinish change was needed, and he found that if getCopyResult() fails with OOM, libpq stays in COPY_IN mode while PQexec() returns NULL, so the next PQexec() fails with "another command is already in progress". Michael Paquier later reported that Heikki could not convince himself the change was sane for the COPY protocol, and planned more testing with tools that use COPY through libpq.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert my bad decision of about a year ago to make PortalDefineQuery responsible for copying the query string into the new Portal.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert my bad decision of about a year ago to make PortalDefineQuery responsible for copying the query string into the new Portal.  Such copying is unnecessary in the common code path through exec_simple_query, and in this case it can be enormously expensive because the string might contain a large number of individual commands; we were copying the entire, long string for each command, resulting in O(N^2) behavior for N commands. (This is the cause of bug #4079.)  A second problem with it is that PortalDefineQuery really can't risk error, because if it elog's before having set up the Portal, we will leak the plancache refcount that the caller is trying to hand off to the portal.  So go back to the design in which the caller is responsible for making sure everything is copied into the portal if necessary.

precedents_retrieved.title: File content logging during execution of COPY queries
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, Tom Lane, Stephen Frost
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch proposed logging the data rows read or written by COPY ... FROM and COPY ... TO when log_statement='all', so that workloads using COPY could be fully recorded for replay and benchmarking. After objections it was revised to add a separate boolean parameter, log_copy, to control this.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan and Tom Lane objected that log_statement is meant for logging statements, not data, and that the change would repeat potentially gigabytes of COPY data into the server log. Stephen Frost questioned logging COPY TO data at all, since results of SELECT and RETURNING are not logged, so network capture would still be needed to record all data. The patch's assigned reviewer was reminded to respond, and the commitfest manager then closed the entry as rejected, noting that some people were against the approach.
matched_queries: COPY ignore errors log rejected rows
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It sounds good when you're looking at toy examples,
but not when it means repeating gigabytes of COPY data into the log.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make ON_ERROR_STOP stop on shell script failure
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes psql's ON_ERROR_STOP also stop a script when a shell command run from psql, such as \! false, exits with a failure status. Later versions extend ON_ERROR_STOP with values that choose whether SQL errors, shell failures or both stop the script, and cover other ways to run shell commands (backticks, \g |, \o |, \w |, \copy program).
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying and waited on its author from December 2022, and the author's email address started bouncing. The CF manager closed it as stalled. Reviewers had also questioned the design: Greg Stark found no tests and did not see why the ON_ERROR_STOP_ON, ON_ERROR_STOP_ALL and ON_ERROR_STOP_SHELL values were needed. Corey Huinker noted that the new SHELL_ERROR variable overlaps with the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch hasn't applied for quite some time, has been waiting on author since
December, and the thread has stalled.

precedents_retrieved.title: Split index and table statistics into different types of stats
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch splits the cumulative statistics kind PGSTAT_KIND_RELATION into PGSTAT_KIND_TABLE and a new PGSTAT_KIND_INDEX, with index-specific counting macros and SQL-callable functions. The goal is sensible field names for index stats and lower memory use, since index entries currently carry unused table counters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stalled. Review comments from Andres Freund and Melanie Plageman were still open, and the author put the work on hold until the related "Generate pg_stat_get_xact*() functions with Macros" patch was done. After that patch was committed, no new version came; the CFM returned the entry because it no longer applied and tests failed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch no longer applies (with tests failing when it did), and the thread
has stalled.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: default to ON_ERROR_STOP
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make ON_ERROR_STOP on the default in psql, so a script or a series of -c and -f options stops at the first error and psql returns a nonzero exit status. The regression tests, which exercise failure cases, would run with ON_ERROR_STOP=0.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the change would break far more existing scripts than it would help, because users who want this behavior already set it, and the default is about twenty years too late to change. He compared it to "set -e" in shell scripts, which is also not the default, and suggested documentation changes. Julien Rouhaud returned the entry because no documentation patch followed in the next few weeks.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The number of scripts you will break is far greater
than the number whose behavior will be improved, because people who
wanted this behavior will already be selecting it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Inconsistent error handling in START_REPLICATION command
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Craig Ringer, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the walsender's switch to COPY BOTH mode in START_REPLICATION to after the logical decoding startup callback runs, so errors from the output plugin startup are reported before COPY starts. It also moves the switch for physical replication so a start LSN beyond the flush position errors out first.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas found the server behaviour correct: an ErrorResponse during copy-both mode ends the copy, and the failure seen comes from psql having no copy-both support. Craig Ringer objected that entering COPY BOTH before the startup callback lets plugins send output from that callback later. The author accepted this, and Tom Lane agreed that the lost flexibility for plugins tilted the decision to reject.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So the problem here isn't that the server is doing anything it
shouldn't be doing; the server code is totally legitimate.  It's just
that the client is stupid.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert applying column aliases to the output of whole-row Vars.
Reverted commit(s): Ensure that RowExprs and whole-row Vars produce the expected column names.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
In commit bf7ca1587, I had the bright idea that we could make the
result of a whole-row Var (that is, foo.*) track any column aliases
that had been applied to the FROM entry the Var refers to.  However,
that's not terribly logically consistent, because now the output of
the Var is no longer of the named composite type that the Var claims
to emit.  bf7ca1587 tried to handle that by changing the output
tuple values to be labeled with a blessed RECORD type, but that's
really pretty disastrous: we can wind up storing such tuples onto
disk, whereupon they're not readable by other sessions.

The only practical fix I can see is to give up on what bf7ca1587
tried to do, and say that the column names of tuples produced by
a whole-row Var are always those of the underlying named composite
type, query aliases or no.  While this introduces some inconsistencies,
it removes others, so it's not that awful in the abstract.  What *is*
kind of awful is to make such a behavioral change in a back-patched
bug fix.  But corrupt data is worse, so back-patched it will be.

(A workaround available to anyone who's unhappy about this is to
introduce an extra level of sub-SELECT, so that the whole-row Var is
referring to the sub-SELECT's output and not to a named table type.
Then the Var is of type RECORD to begin with and there's no issue.)

Per report from Miles Delahunty.  The faulty commit dates to 9.5,
so back-patch to all supported branches.

roaster_notes.note: P1 and P2 died because they caught errors with PG_TRY, and this proposal sits on the soft-error path ON_ERROR ignore already uses. P8 logged all COPY data to the server log, while this proposal stores only failed rows in a table the user chose. Message #1 cites an earlier Tom Lane suggestion by link only, so the material does not show its content.
WAL, standby, wire protocol and the ExecInsert export add no new cross-node state, so they raise nothing from this angle.

One objection, on trigger execution context. Leaks of raw input lines go only to a table the COPY user chose, so they are not raised. Unbounded error-table growth comes from the user's own input, so it is not raised as a denial of service.
Hot-path cost seems limited to users of ON_ERROR table, but the proposal gives no numbers, and v15's switch to CIM_SINGLE in some cases is not explained.
One objection only. Other workarounds, such as capturing LOG_VERBOSITY verbose NOTICEs on the client or using external loaders, are weaker substitutes, so they are not raised separately.
Two objections raised. The demand objection is a not-now case: it asks for field evidence and does not argue that the feature is a bad idea.
